nodes.name: Additive-Ionomer Interphase Formation
nodes.procedure: When the transparent, yellowish PiperION anion-exchange ionomer dispersion is added to Zr(OPr)₄, the mixture turns milky white (fig. S1) as the metal alkoxides partially hydrolyze, Zr(OPr)₄ + H₂O→ Zr(OH)(OPr)₃ + PrOH, and react with the bicarbonate counterions, Zr(OPr)₄ + HCO₃⁻ → Zr(OPr)₃(CO₃)⁻ + PrOH. These new species condense to form oligomers, e.g., via Zr(OPr)₃(OH) + Zr(OPr)₃(OH)→ Zr(OPr)₃ - O - Zr(OPr)₃ + H₂O. Simultaneously, the hydrolyzed inorganic species interact with the organic ionomers, forming chemical cross-links. The resulting inorganic oligomer-ionomer dispersion is then coated at 80°C onto the anode catalysts (here typically CoOₓ based) that are grown directly on a Ni or steel porous transport layer (PTL). As alcohol and water evaporate, polycondensation is promoted and a cross-linked inorganic-organic hybrid interphase that has improved oxidative resistance and mechanical adhesion is formed (Fig. 1C).

nodes.description: Three-electrode OER activity test in 0.10 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Counterintuitively, three-electrode measurements in 0.10 M KOH showed that coating e-Co(OH)2 with the Zr propoxide additive enhanced the water-oxidation activity by ∼8% (fig.S17).

nodes.description: Three-electrode OER measurement in 0.10 M KOH with Zr additive coating
nodes.source_text: three-electrode measurements in 0.10 M KOH showed that coating e-Co(OH)2 with the Zr propoxide additive enhanced the water-oxidation activity by ∼8% (fig.S17). The improvement may be due to ZrOx modifying the catalyst surface chemistry, perhaps increasing hydrophilicity under oxygen evolution reaction conditions (fig.S18)

nodes.characterization_summary: Low-dose cryo-TEM of e-Co(OH)₂-additives-ionomer interphase shows distinct nanometer-scale dark features consistent with ZrOₓ dispersed in the ionomer near the catalyst surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Low-dose cryo-transmission electron microscopy (cryo-TEM) was used to study the system... The sample with additive displayed distinct, nanometer-scale, dark features within the ionomer and near the e-Co(OH)₂ catalyst surface, which we attributed to amorphous ZrOₓ rich regions.

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS of the e-Co(OH)₂-additive-ionomer sample shows the Zr L-edge, which was not present in the control sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) of the e-Co(OH)₂-additive-ionomer sample (fig. S40) showed the Zr L-edge, which was not present in the control sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cross-sectional SEM images and EDX maps of Zr show uniform distribution in pristine e-Co(OH)₂-additives-ionomer samples on PTLs, with Zr enrichment next to the electrocatalyst after 1 hour of operation at 2.0 A cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cross-sectional maps (Fig. 3, C to F, and figs. S42 to S45) showed Zr uniformly distributed in the pristine samples. After 1 hour of operation at 2.0 A cm⁻², increased Zr was found in the regions next to the electrocatalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows continuous loss of ionomer on catalyst surface in ionomer-only system vs. additives-ionomer interphase remaining adhered to electrocatalyst surface after 20 hours at 2.0 A cm⁻² (figs. S34 and S35).
nodes.evidence_snippet: For cells with optimal Zr(OPr)₄, the additives-ionomer interphase layer remained adhered to the electrocatalyst surface even after 20 hours at 2.0 A cm⁻² (figs. S34 and S35).

nodes.characterization_summary: Time-of-flight secondary-ion mass spectrometry depth profiles showed a uniform distribution of ZrOₓ and ionomer in films coated on flat iridium-coated silicon control wafer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Time-of-flight secondary-ion mass spectrometry depth profiles showed a uniform distribution of ZrOₓ and ionomer in films coated on a flat iridium-coated silicon control wafer (fig. S41).
